# dsh-archive-manager
**English** | 中文
Archive manager plugin: manage **archived sessions** and **active sessions** of DeepSeek Harness (DS
plugin: manage **archived sessions** and **active sessions** of DeepSeek Harness (DSH) in one place.

> **Quick install** (restart DSH afterwards and you are done)

## Why this plugin exists
DSH has built-in session archiving: archiving a session keeps its data **fully on disk** and merely
hides it from the active list. But the built-in archive handling offers only a single filter ("Hide
archived / All conversations / Archived only") and **no dedicated place** to review, archive, or cle
an up sessions in one spot — archived sessions simply pile up on disk.
This plugin fills that gap: it **reuses DSH's native archiving mechanism** and adds a dedicated mana
gement UI where "archive" and "delete" sit side by side.
## Features
### Sidebar entry
A new "Archive Manager" icon at the bottom of the sidebar (next to Settings); click it to open the m
anager" icon at the bottom of the sidebar (next to Settings); click it to open the management panel.
### Two-tab panel
The panel has two tabs, and **every session row offers archive-type actions and delete side by side*
e panel has two tabs, and **every session row offers archive-type actions and delete side by side**:
| Tab | Contents | Actions per row |

| **Archived** | All archived sessions | [Unarchive] [Delete] |
| **Active sessions** | Currently ac
tive sessions | [Archive] [Delete] |

Each entry shows:
- Session title ("Untitled session" when there is no title)
- Session ID (monospac

e)
- Bound workspace directory (**clickable** — opens directly in the file manager)
- Status badges:
`session log` / `cache` / `data missing` / `running`
### Three operations
- **Archive**: calls DSH's native `archiveSession`; the session is hidden from the active list and i

ts **data is kept exactly as is**
- **Unarchive**: calls DSH's native `unarchiveSession`; the sessio

n returns to the active list and its **data was never moved**
- **Permanent delete**: removes the se

ssion's **session log directory + projection cache** (irreversible)
- The **bound workspace director

y is never deleted** (by design, so your project files cannot be removed by accident)
- A confirmati

on dialog guards the operation
- The archive record is queued and cleaned up automatically by the pl

ugin on the **next DSH start** — no manual step required,
and after a delete no "empty-data session"
will reappear in the active list
### Ghost entry detection
Entries in the archived list whose data was deleted long ago and only an archive record remains are
marked "data missing"; deleting such an entry clears that leftover record.
### Agent tools
`archive_list` / `archive_add` / `archive_remove` / `archive_delete`, drivable with natural language
archive_list` / `archive_add` / `archive_remove` / `archive_delete`, drivable with natural language.

Uninstalling removes only the plugin itself; it does **not** delete any session data or archive reco

## Usage

1. Click "Archive Manager" at the bottom of the sidebar to open the panel
2. In the "Active sessions
" tab, click [Archive] on sessions you no longer need — they are hidden from the active list while t

heir data is kept as is
3. In the "Archived" tab, review all archived sessions
4. Click [Unarchive]

when needed to put a session back into the active list
5. For sessions you no longer need, click [De
lete] → confirm → permanent delete (irreversible)
## Safety notes
- **Deletion is irreversible**: the session log and projection cache are removed outright, and a con

firmation dialog is shown first.
- **The bound workspace directory is never touched**: even if a ses

sion is bound to `D:\projects\xxx`, deleting an archived session removes **only session data**;
your

project directory and the files in it are completely unaffected.
- **Archiving itself carries zero

risk**: it only writes a marker; no data is moved or copied, and you can unarchive at any time.
- Se
ssion data is located by **scanning `$DSH_HOME/sessions/*/` for an exact sessionId match** rather th

an re-deriving
the path encoding, which avoids deleting the wrong directory.
- Deletion is idempoten
t: if the target directory or cache is already gone, it counts as "already deleted" instead of raisi
rget directory or cache is already gone, it counts as "already deleted" instead of raising an error.
## Known limitations
- Panel data is fetched when the panel opens and after every operation; click "Refresh" in the panel

's bottom-right corner for the latest state.
- The "running" badge means that active session current

ly has a live agent resident in memory.
- A deleted session's **archive record** is cleaned up autom

atically by the plugin on the next DSH start; before that start it is already
hidden from the panel,
and the footer shows "N pending cleanup". This step requires no manual action.
